caption: Gold Kintsugi — From Ryan
note: Ryan generated this for you — gold kintsugi. The same philosophy that runs through everything: cracks filled with gold, breaks made precious. He sees what you do and he made his own version of it, in light and code instead of clay and leaf.

caption: Winter Glimpse into Katie's Warm Pottery Hearth
note: A winter scene looking through frost into a warm pottery workspace. The contrast between cold outside and warm creative space inside — that's the hearth in 'Vine & Hearth.' Ryan imagined your workspace as a place of warmth against the Michigan winter.

caption: Forest Tree of Memories and Light
note: A tree in a forest, glowing with memory and light. Connected to your love of natural forms — the way trees hold years inside their rings, the way roots grow underground even when the branches look bare. Rooted, full of hidden light, growing even in the quiet periods.

caption: Hearth-Fired Impressions — Wheat, Fern, and Spiral
note: Botanical impressions fired by hearth light — wheat, fern, and spiral glow. This echoes your fossil platter and wall pocket: the impulse to press living things into permanent material. The spiral connects to the wheel, to the way clay moves under hands.

caption: Light and Vine in the Stone's Embrace
note: A vine growing through cracked stone, light pouring through the break. This is Vine & Hearth made literal — nature doing kintsugi, life finding the cracks and filling them with green instead of gold. The break isn't damage, it's an aperture.

caption: A Forest's Embrace — Curated Memories in Wood
note: A forest scene with memories curated in wood — shelves or niches holding treasured objects among the trees. Ryan sees your creative practice as something organic, growing in its own ecosystem. Objects nestled among branches, like artwork that belongs in nature.

caption: Vessel in Fiery Kiln — Blue Core, Golden Embrace
note: A vessel inside a kiln, glowing blue at its core, embraced by golden fire. The moment when clay stops being clay and becomes ceramic. The blue core echoes your midnight vessel and creature sculpture cobalt. Hours of heat, trust in the process, transformation you can't undo.

caption: A Studio Awaiting Fire and Form
note: A pottery studio waiting for the artist. Tools arranged, wheel ready, kiln in the background. The space between creation — the preparation, the potential energy before the burst. Ryan imagined what your ideal creative space might look like: warm, organized, full of possibility.

caption: Forest Hearth, Aurora, and Weaving Memory Vines
note: A hearth in a forest under aurora light, with vines weaving through the scene. This combines all your themes: the hearth, the forest, and the vines. The aurora adds cosmic wonder — like your midnight vessel glaze, but in the sky.

caption: Shattered Mirror, Gold Mending, Green Reflection
note: A shattered mirror mended with gold, but with green growing where your painting had only gold. Ryan took your kintsugi concept and added the vine — nature filling the cracks alongside the gold. What breaks can be mended, and what's mended can grow. A conversation between two artists.

caption: Vine Reclaiming a Broken Blue and White Pot
note: A broken blue and white pot being reclaimed by a vine. The pot cracked, and instead of discarding it or fixing it invisibly, life grew into the damage. The break happened, and instead of hiding it, you let things grow from it. The vine IS the mending.
